outlook: Grains closed lower on Election Day: December corn fell 6¾ cents to $4.41½, January soybeans slipped 3¼ cents to $12.13½ and December Chicago wheat dropped 7¾ cents to $5.98¾, while December Minneapolis spring wheat was down about 4¼ cents near $6.21½ at midday. Wheat was pressured by news that the U.S. will host Russia–Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10–11, which traders see as possibly freeing up more Black Sea grain. USDA's Monday Crop Progress report put corn harvest at 74% complete (77% five-year average) and soybeans at 88% (84% average), and USDA confirmed a 1.73 million-tonne corn sale to Mexico and 136,000 tonnes of soybeans to China. September soybean crush of 198.8 million bushels came in below trade expectations.
